title: Window Cleaning Prices UK 2026 | Local Price Guide
description: Check window cleaning prices in your area. Compare regular, first-clean, inside and conservatory costs or enter your postcode for a local estimate.
heading: Window Cleaning Prices UK
intro:
Window cleaning prices vary enormously depending on the actual windows, how often they're cleaned, access and where you live.

Use our local price checker for a quick guide, or calculate the whole property for a more accurate estimate.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

sections.heading: How much does window cleaning cost?

blocks.text:
For a normal regular window cleaning round, many homes will fall somewhere from the low teens into £30 or more per visit.

Smaller properties in lower-priced areas can be cheaper. Large detached homes, premium locations, difficult access, three-storey properties and homes with lots of glass can cost considerably more.

The most important thing is that the price should reflect the actual work involved.

A small terrace with six easy windows should not automatically cost the same as another terrace with bays, French doors, Velux windows and awkward rear access.

sections.heading: Window cleaning prices by property type

blocks.text: Property type is useful as a rough starting point, but it should never be the only thing used to calculate the price.
Flats and apartments

A small ground-floor flat can be a relatively quick clean, especially where all of the glass is accessible from outside.

Flats can become much more expensive when balconies, restricted access or windows that can only be reached through the property are involved.
Terraced houses

Terraced homes are often among the quickest regular jobs when the fronts and backs are straightforward.

The price can change significantly where rear access is through the house, there are large extensions at the back or the property has bay windows.
Semi-detached houses

Semis are one of the most common regular window cleaning jobs in the UK.

The total usually comes down to the number of windows, doors and any extras rather than the fact the house happens to be semi-detached.
Detached houses

Detached houses often have more side windows and more glass overall, so they usually cost more than a comparable terrace or semi.

Large bifold doors, roof windows and extensions can increase the price further.
Bungalows

Bungalows can be straightforward because everything is at ground level, but they often have more windows spread around the building.

A bungalow with twenty windows can still be a bigger job than a two-storey house with ten.
Large homes and estates

Large homes should be priced around the amount of glass and the time required rather than being forced into a normal house-price bracket.

Our calculator allows you to count individual window types so larger properties can be priced properly.

sections.heading: How much does window cleaning cost per window?

blocks.text:
A simple price per window can be useful when you are trying to understand a quote, but it does not tell the whole story.

A small bathroom window is not the same job as a large picture window.

A normal casement window is not the same as a large bay.

A Velux can take more work than a straightforward ground-floor window.

There is also normally a minimum visit price.

This means four windows will not necessarily cost half as much as eight windows because the cleaner still has to travel to the property, set up the equipment and complete the job.

Regular window cleaning is normally cheaper per visit when the cleaner is coming more often.

A four-weekly customer is giving the cleaner regular work and the windows do not usually have as much time to build up dirt.

At six or eight weeks, the job may take a little longer and the cleaner is earning from that property fewer times during the year.

Twelve-weekly and occasional cleans will normally carry a larger increase.

One-off cleans are different again and are usually priced considerably higher than a regular maintenance visit.

sections.heading: Why does the first window clean cost more?

blocks.text:
A first clean is normally more work.

The cleaner may need to remove old dirt from the glass, frames and sills before the property can be maintained properly.

There may be algae around the seals, heavy dirt on the frames, old cobwebs, bird mess and areas that need rinsing several times.

For this reason, our calculator does not treat the first clean as just another normal visit.

The first clean starts higher than the regular price and can increase further where the windows have not been professionally cleaned for a long time.

Inside window cleaning should not automatically be cheaper than the outside.

The cleaner has to move around the house, work around furniture, blinds and curtains, protect the inside of the property and normally clean the glass using traditional tools.

For some cleaners, inside work takes longer than the exterior.

That is why our calculator prices inside cleaning separately.

There is a huge difference between cleaning a few conservatory side panes and cleaning an entire conservatory inside and out.

A full conservatory clean can include:

side glass
doors
frames
outside roof panels
inside glass
inside roof panels
roof bars and awkward detailed areas

Inside conservatory roofs can be particularly time-consuming.

Our calculator treats conservatory work as a separate part of the job instead of simply adding a few pounds to the house price.

sections.heading: Does your postcode affect window cleaning prices?

blocks.text:
Yes.
Window cleaning prices are not the same everywhere in the UK.

Local house prices can affect what the market will support, but they are not the only factor.

Parking, congestion, travel time, emissions restrictions, route density and local competition all make a difference.

There are also places that do not follow the normal regional pattern.

Some premium rural and tourist locations can be expensive even though they are nowhere near London.

Some parts of the South Wales Valleys can be much cheaper than the UK average.

That is why our calculator uses postcode information rather than giving the whole country the same price.

sections.heading: What affects a window cleaning quote?

blocks.text: Number of windows
More glass normally means more time.
Window size
Large panes and doors usually take longer than small windows.
Height
Third and fourth-floor work can require more time and care.
Access
Windows over extensions, behind obstacles or accessed through the house can increase the price.
Frequency
Less frequent cleaning normally costs more per visit.
Condition
A maintained property is different from a first clean that has not been done for several years.
Inside cleaning
Inside windows are their own job and should be priced separately.
Location
The same property can have a different market price depending on where it is.

title: Commercial Window Cleaning Cost UK | Pricing Guide
description: See what affects commercial window cleaning costs for shops, offices, schools and larger buildings, including access, height and cleaning frequency.
heading: Commercial Window Cleaning Cost UK
intro:
Commercial window cleaning needs a different pricing system from normal residential work.

A shopfront cleaned every week is very different from a school, hotel or office building.

This is why we are building commercial pricing separately rather than forcing commercial jobs into the domestic calculator.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

sections.heading: What affects commercial window cleaning prices?

blocks.text: The main factors are:
Amount of glass
Building height
Frequency
Access method
Site rules
Parking
Working hours
Pedestrian management
Inside cleaning
specialist equipment

Small shopfronts are normally among the simplest commercial jobs.

Frequent weekly or fortnightly cleaning can keep the price per visit relatively low.

Large panes, internal glass and awkward parking can increase it.

Office pricing depends heavily on the building.

A low-rise office with easy water-fed pole access can be straightforward.

A multi-storey office requiring specialist access is a completely different contract.

Larger sites are normally quoted after a site survey.

The cleaner needs to understand where vehicles can park, what areas are accessible, whether the work must be completed at certain times and whether any additional site paperwork is required.

MEWP work, rope access and other specialist systems should never be priced using a normal residential per-window figure.

Equipment, training and risk all need to be included.

title: Conservatory Cleaning Cost UK | Roof, Inside & Outside
description: See conservatory cleaning prices for side glass, outside roofs, internal glass and inside roof cleaning. Calculate the different parts of your job.
heading: Conservatory Cleaning Cost UK
intro:
“Conservatory cleaning” can mean two completely different things.

One customer may only want the exterior side glass cleaned.

Another may want every pane, frame and roof section cleaned inside and out.

That is why conservatory prices can range from a relatively small add-on to several hundred pounds.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

blocks.text:
Exterior side glass is normally the simplest part of the job.

Small and medium panes can be priced in a similar way to normal windows.

Large floor-to-ceiling conservatory panels should cost more.

A conservatory roof should normally be priced separately from the side glass.

The cleaner needs to work across multiple roof panels and often has to deal with algae, moss and dirt around the roof bars.

Larger and more complex roof shapes take longer.

Inside conservatories can be much slower than the exterior.

Furniture, blinds and awkward angles all matter.

The cleaner also needs to be careful with water inside the customer's home.
This is where conservatory cleaning can become expensive.
Internal roof glass is difficult to reach.
The cleaner may need to reposition steps or a platform repeatedly.
Roof bars, angles and finials all slow the job down.
Blinds can make the work even harder.
This should never be treated as a small add-on.

A first clean normally means the customer intends to continue with regular cleaning afterwards.

A one-off clean means the cleaner may never return.

That matters.

Regular customers give the cleaner future work, while a one-off customer has to carry the full travel and setup cost in one visit.

This is why one-off pricing can sometimes be higher again.

title: Conservatory Roof Cleaning Cost UK | Price Per Panel
description: See conservatory roof cleaning costs, including exterior, inside and per-panel pricing. Find out what changes the price and calculate your conservatory.
heading: Conservatory Roof Cleaning Cost
intro:
Conservatory roof cleaning should be priced around the roof itself, not simply added to the normal window cleaning price.

The number of roof panels, condition and roof design all matter.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

blocks.text:
An exterior roof clean normally has a minimum charge because the cleaner has to prepare specifically for the roof work.

After that, the number and size of panels increase the price.

A small maintained roof can be relatively straightforward.

A large green roof that has not been cleaned for years is a completely different job.

Per-panel pricing can be useful, particularly for larger roofs.

However, the cleaner should still have a starting or setup price.

Ten panels at £5 per panel does not automatically mean a £50 total if the roof requires considerable setup and detailed work.

Inside roofs normally cost more than exterior roofs.

The cleaner is working at awkward angles and has less freedom to use water.

Furniture and blinds may also be directly underneath the work.

Glass roof panels can normally be cleaned to a clearer visual finish.

Polycarbonate roofs can still be cleaned, but the expectations are different and the material may show age or staining that cleaning cannot completely remove.

IVictorian, Edwardian, P-shaped and other complex conservatories contain more angles and roof bars than a simple lean-to.

More complexity generally means more time.

sections.heading: How often should a conservatory roof be cleaned?

blocks.text:
For many homes, once or twice a year is enough to stop heavy algae and grime building up.

Properties under trees or in damp areas may need attention more often.

title: First Window Clean Cost UK | Why First Cleans Cost More
description: Find out how much a first window clean should cost, why it costs more than regular cleaning and how condition affects the initial price.
heading: How Much Should a First Window Clean Cost?
intro:
A first window clean usually costs more than the regular maintenance clean.

This is not simply because the cleaner is new to the property.

The first visit is normally where the difficult work happens.

Once the glass, frames and sills have been brought up to a good standard, future regular cleans should be quicker.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

sections.heading: How Much Should a First Window Clean Cost?

blocks.text: A first clean may involve:
Built-up dirt
Old cobwebs
Bird mess
Algae around frames
Dirty sills
Years of grime
Extra rinsing
More detailed frame work
On a regular maintenance visit, most of this heavy work has already been dealt with.

A first clean normally means the customer intends to continue with regular cleaning afterwards.

A one-off clean means the cleaner may never return.

That matters.

Regular customers give the cleaner future work, while a one-off customer has to carry the full travel and setup cost in one visit.

This is why one-off pricing can sometimes be higher again.

sections.heading: How condition affects the first clean

blocks.text: Recently maintained
A modest first-clean increase may be enough.
Several months since the last clean
More frame and sill work may be required.
One year or more
The cleaner should expect a noticeable difference from a maintenance clean.
Several years
The first clean can become a restoration-style job and should be priced accordingly.

title: How Our Window Cleaning Price Calculator Works
description: See how Window Cleaning Calculator estimates prices using window types, minimum charges, frequency, access, first cleans, location and more.
heading: How Our Window Cleaning Calculator Works
intro:
Window Cleaning Calculator is designed to give a more useful estimate than simply asking how many bedrooms a property has.

A bedroom count does not tell us how much glass needs to be cleaned.

Our calculator looks at the actual job.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

blocks.text:
Different window types have different values.

Small windows sit at the bottom.

Standard windows create the main base price.

Large windows, bays, Velux windows, sash windows, bifold panels and other detailed glazing increase the job value.

Every cleaner has costs before the first piece of glass is cleaned.

Travel.

Fuel.

Van costs.

Equipment.

Purified water.

Admin.

Time.

That is why very small jobs normally hit a minimum visit price.

A normal two-storey house is the baseline.

Three and four-storey work can take longer.

Access can also change the job.

A property with easy front and rear access is different from a property where the cleaner has to carry equipment through the house.

Four-weekly cleaning is the baseline regular service.

Six, eight and twelve-weekly cleaning gradually increases the price per visit.

One-off work is priced differently because the cleaner may not return to the property again.

The calculator gives the first clean its own price.

A first clean starts at a minimum increase over the regular maintenance price.

The increase becomes larger where the windows are neglected.

Inside windows are calculated separately.

We do not assume inside cleaning should be cheaper than outside cleaning.

The calculator also considers how difficult the internal access is.

Window cleaners can tell us whether they are quick, average or slower at inside cleaning so the suggested quote does not leave them undercharging for their time.

Conservatories have their own pricing system.

Side glass.

Outside roofs.

Inside glass.

Inside roofs.

Each section can have a different price.

The calculator then adjusts the estimate using the location.

This is based on the local pricing market and, where relevant, the extra cost of working in dense urban areas.

The goal is not to say every house in an expensive postcode must cost a fortune.

The location adjustment is deliberately capped.

The actual glass still matters more.

Window cleaners using the calculator can tell us what they would actually charge.

We use this feedback to spot places where our model may be too high or too low.

We do not automatically allow one person's answer to change the calculator.

Changes are reviewed before being added to future versions.

title: Inside Window Cleaning Cost UK | Inside & Outside Prices
description: Check inside window cleaning prices and see why internal cleaning can cost as much as the outside. Calculate inside and outside costs for your home.
heading: Inside Window Cleaning Cost UK
intro:
Inside window cleaning is often underpriced.

It looks easier because the cleaner is standing indoors, but in reality it can take as long as the exterior and sometimes longer.

This is why our calculator never assumes the inside should automatically cost less than the outside..
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

sections.heading: Why does inside window cleaning cost so much?

blocks.text:
Outside, a water-fed pole cleaner can often work continuously around the building.
Inside, everything changes.
The cleaner has to enter each room.
Furniture may need to be worked around.
Blinds and curtains can restrict access.
Items may be sitting on the windowsill.
The glass normally needs to be cleaned and detailed by hand.
That all takes time.
On a regular maintenance visit, most of this heavy work has already been dealt with.

sections.heading: Should inside windows cost the same as outside?

blocks.text:
As a starting point, we think inside cleaning should be worth at least as much as the equivalent exterior work.

For a straightforward home, our calculator normally puts inside work slightly above the exterior labour value.

Where access is difficult, the inside price increases further.

sections.heading: What makes inside cleaning more expensive?

blocks.text: Furniture
Large sofas, beds and desks can make the glass difficult to reach.
Blinds
Cleaning around blinds can slow the job considerably.
Ornaments and windowsills
The cleaner should not have to spend half the appointment moving somebody's belongings.
Detailed glazing
Leaded, Georgian and sash windows usually need more hand work.

sections.heading: How often should inside windows be cleaned?

blocks.text:
Many people do not need the inside cleaned every time the exterior is done.

Common choices include:

Every exterior visit
Every second visit
Every few months
One-off when required

Your cleaner may charge slightly more per inside clean when the gap between visits is longer.

If you clean professionally, your speed matters.

A cleaner who is very quick with an applicator and squeegee can complete internal work much faster than somebody still developing their technique.

Our cleaner calculator asks about this because a slow inside job should not leave you earning half your normal hourly rate.

title: One-Off Window Cleaning Cost UK | Check Your Price
description: See how much one-off window cleaning costs, why it costs more than regular cleaning and calculate a one-time clean for your property.
heading: One-Off Window Cleaning Cost UK
intro:
A one-off window clean is normally more expensive than joining a regular cleaning round.

The cleaner is travelling to the property for one job with no guarantee of future work.

The windows may also be dirtier than a property that is maintained every four, six or eight weeks.
Free to use · No account needed · Local pricing

sections.heading: How much does a one-off window clean cost?

blocks.text:
The final price depends on the number of windows, condition, access and location.

A small one-off job may still hit the cleaner's minimum charge.

Larger properties can quickly move into £30, £40, £50 or more.

Inside cleaning and conservatories are normally additional.

sections.heading: Why are one-off cleans more expensive?

blocks.text:
Regular window cleaning is efficient.

The cleaner knows the property, knows the access and can often group the job with other customers nearby.

A one-off clean does not have the same advantage.

The cleaner may be making a special journey for that one property.

A first clean and a one-off clean can look similar.

The difference is what happens next.

A first clean usually leads into a regular four, six or eight-week service.

A one-off clean finishes after the first visit.

That can justify a higher price.

If you want both sides of the glass cleaned, expect the cost to increase significantly.

Inside cleaning is not just a quick add-on.

The cleaner has to move through the property and work around furniture, curtains and blinds.
